Operator: Good morning, and welcome to the Apex Energy Corp Q3 2024 Earnings Conference Call. All participants will be in listen-only mode. After today's presentation, there will be an opportunity to ask questions. [Operator Instructions] Please note this event is being recorded.

I would now like to turn the conference over to Alex Rivera, Vice President of Investor Relations. Please go ahead.

Alex Rivera: Thank you, Operator, and good morning, everyone. Welcome to Apex Energy Corp's Q3 2024 earnings call. Joining me on the call today are Mark Harlan, Chief Executive Officer; Elena Vasquez, Chief Financial Officer; and Tom Reilly, Chief Operating Officer.

Before we begin, I would like to remind you that some of the statements we make today may be forward-looking. These statements are based on current expectations and assumptions and are subject to risks and uncertainties that could cause actual results to differ materially. Please refer to our SEC filings for a more detailed discussion of these risks.

I will now turn the call over to Mark Harlan.

Mark Harlan: Thank you, Alex, and good morning, everyone. Apex Energy Corp delivered solid results in Q3, driven by strong operational performance and favorable commodity prices. We achieved record production volumes averaging 248,000 barrels of oil equivalent per day, up 18.7% year-over-year. I'm particularly pleased with our progress on ESG initiatives, including substantial advancements in emissions reduction targets. We are focused on disciplined capital expenditure guidance to drive high returns across our portfolio. Finally, we are taking steps to optimize our capital allocation priorities, balancing sustainable dividends, share buybacks, and strategic reinvestment.

Now, I'll turn the call over to Elena Vasquez to discuss our financial results in more detail.

Elena Vasquez: Thank you, Mark. As Mark highlighted, we had a strong quarter. Our revenue was $2.45 billion, up 25% year-over-year. Operating income was $820 million, and net income was $610 million. We generated $680 million in free cash flow and returned $420 million to shareholders through dividends and share repurchases. Our balance sheet remains strong, with $4.2 billion in debt and $1.5 billion in cash.

Let me now provide some additional color on our capital expenditure guidance for the rest of 2024 and looking into 2025. This reflects our disciplined approach to deploying capital in a supportive market backdrop, where Brent has held steady around $82 per barrel and WTI near $78, backed by sustained OPEC+ cuts and solid demand from Asian markets. We're set up to generate attractive returns while pushing forward our multi-year plans.

For the full year 2024, we're holding our CapEx outlook at $5.8 billion, which is about 12% above last year's $5.2 billion figure, tied to elevated drilling and completion activity in our premier assets and targeted expansion plays. This equates to roughly 45% of our expected full-year adjusted free cash flow of $12.9 billion based on current forwards, keeping leverage comfortably under 1.0x net debt to EBITDA and maintaining plenty of flexibility.

Moving into 2025, we see CapEx landing between $6.0 billion and $6.4 billion, centered at the midpoint barring big M&A moves or price swings, with emphasis on initiatives that yield quick paybacks.

Breaking it out by bucket and geography:

Upstream development takes $3.6 billion, or 62% of the pot, fueling drilling and completions on our top-tier drilling locations. In the Permian, across our 450,000 net acres in the Delaware and Midland, that's $2.1 billion—an 18% jump from last year—for 320 gross operated wells, aiming for 15% production growth to 450,000 boe/d by year-end. We're running multi-well pads with laterals stretching to 12,000 feet on average, powered by our Cube fracking system that's ramped proppant to 2,500 pounds per foot, boosting initial rates 22% over prior years. These deliver IRRs of 28% to 35% at $70 WTI, half-cycle paybacks under 10 months, and breakevens down to $42 a barrel due to efficiency gains and owned midstream in the basin.

Overseas, $850 million goes to Guyana offshore in the Stabroek Block joint venture, accelerating Phase 3 like ExxonMobil's Liza and Payara, with two FPSOs coming online mid-2025 for 150,000 barrels per day gross. IRRs top 30% at $75 Brent with sub-$5 breakevens. North Sea gets $650 million for Buzzard field upgrades, including polymer EOR tests lifting recovery to 42% from 35%.

Exploration and appraisal CapEx is $850 million, or 15%. That includes $450 million for key wildcats, $250 million in Permian hybrid source-rock prospects akin to Pioneer's wins, targeting 10-15% reserve replacement. Namibia offshore sees $200 million for Graff-1X appraisal post-Venus find, similar to TotalEnergies' light oil, with upside to 1 billion boe recoverable and success odds over 40%. We only pull triggers on prospects with unrisked NAV over $20 per barrel and post-drill IRRs above 25%.

Maintenance, midstream, and corporate rounds out at $900 million, or 15%. Base upkeep and integrity on our 25,000-mile pipes and 12 gas facilities is $550 million for 99% reliability. Midstream $250 million expands Permian egress, like our 20% in the Matterhorn Express with Kinder Morgan, trimming basis to under 50 cents per MMBtu.

Low-carbon efforts get $450 million, or 8%, supporting net-zero by 2050. That's $250 million for Permian CCUS tied to Occidental's Stratos DAC hub, plus $100 million electrifying rigs with nat-gas gensets, trimming Scope 1 by 25%. CCUS is showing 12-15% IRRs from 45Q credits and EOR, with NPV10 over $500 million.

Our mix prioritizes velocity—85% on spots with D&C under $7 million per well and 10+ years inventory at 5% decline. Versus ConocoPhillips or EOG, our Permian FCF breakeven at $48 per barrel ranks top quartile per Rystad. Returns over volume: nothing below 20% IRR hurdle, with 50-60% FCF back to owners via buybacks and our dividend yielding 3.2%.

Service inflation at 5% YoY and Guyana regs are watches, but AI seismic cuts dry holes 15%, and hedges cover 60% 2025 oil at $75. At $70 WTI, we'd trim 2024 CapEx to $5.4 billion; at $90, add 10% to exp.

This sets up 18-22% portfolio returns, 8% output growth to 1.1 million boe/d, and de-risks 8 billion boe inventory over 15 years.

Shifting to capital allocation priorities, which drive our edge in total shareholder returns amid choppy oil dynamics. With Brent at $82 this quarter—8% above last year on OPEC+ discipline and Asia strength—we posted $2.8 billion FCF at guidance midpoint. This funds our trio of pillars: growing dividends first, smart buybacks, and prudent organic reinvestment.

Dividends lead: eight straight quarterly hikes, today's 12% bump to $0.85 per share quarterly ($3.40 annual) yields 4.7% forward—beating ExxonMobil's 3.8% and Chevron's 4.2%, fueled by 95% FCF conversion. Payout at 35% of FCF trails the 45% peer norm, with $4.2 billion slated for 2024 dividends, up 15% YoY. This backs our Permian breakevens at $35 WTI for downside protection.

Buybacks next: shares at 7.2x EV/EBITDA (vs. 6.8x S&P Oil & Gas) scream value. Q3 wrapped $1.1 billion of our $3 billion program, retiring 4.2 million shares for 3% TTM EPS lift. We dialed back in Q2 sub-$70 WTI, hedging instead at $75-85 for 60% 2024 oil. Unlike Occidental's post-deal binge, we peg 25-30% FCF here under 10% FCF yield. 2024 target: $2.5-3 billion, possibly 8-10% float if prices steady.

Reinvestment closes the loop, targeting 5-7% CAGR output through 2030. 35-40% FCF to $6.5 billion CapEx in 2024, all >15% ROIC. 70% Permian: 40 Eagle Ford/Wolfcamp wells per rig on 1.2 million acres, Q3 pads hitting 1,800 boe/d 30-day IP (20% over curve) via 4,500 lbs/ft proppant and diverters, 12-day cycles.

Beyond Lower 48, 15% CapEx to Brazil pre-salt Santos like Petrobras, Phase 2 FPSO next year adds 50,000 boe/d at $25/boe. Suriname Block 58 appraisal de-risks 500 million barrels with SLB digital twins, 25% less dry risk.

Energy transition: 10% or $650 million to CCUS/low-carbon—Permian CO2 hub at 2 MMtpa by 2026 for 45Q and blue H2 like Occidental/1PointFive.

Dynamic toggles: $60 WTI shifts 50% to returns; $80+ flexes reinvestment to 45%. $8 billion liquidity, zero net debt. Blends ConocoPhillips M&A and EOG organic for 18% 5-year TSR, 500 bps over XLE.

Dividends steady, buybacks accretive, reinvestment compounds 10%+ ROCE in tight supply/LNG world—not volume chases, per-share value.

I will now turn the call over to Tom Reilly for an operational update.

Tom Reilly: Thank you, Elena. Operationally, we're executing our strategy with precision. Our production averaged 248,000 barrels of oil equivalent per day in Q3. This marked a 4.2% increase quarter-over-quarter from 238,000 BOE/d in Q2 and a strong 18.7% rise year-over-year from 209,000 BOE/d last Q3. We beat our guidance range of 240,000 to 245,000 BOE/d thanks to better-than-anticipated well results and very little unplanned downtime.

By commodity: Oil hit 172,000 barrels per day, 69% of the mix—up 5.1% QoQ from 163,700 bbl/d on 28 new D&C wells in the Permian's Delaware Basin. YoY, that's 22.4% growth from 140,600 bbl/d, powered by 2023 buys like the $450 million Midland bolt-on adding 15,000 bbl/d low-decline.

Gas was 456,000 Mcf per day, converting to 76,000 BOE/d at 6:1 (31% total)—1.8% QoQ from 448,000 Mcf/d on Permian associated gas, offset by curtailments at weak $2.15 Henry Hub (down 15% QoQ). YoY up 10.2% from 414,000 Mcf/d via Eagle Ford NGL-rich, 12 new wells over 25 MMcf/d IP.

Oil cut rose to 69% from 65% YoY, intentional via Tier 1 focus (75% D&C spend). Declines 12-15% annual, managed by infills and comps.

Regionally: Permian (72%, 179,000 BOE/d) up 6.8% QoQ, oil 132,000 bbl/d—four Delaware pads on VanguardMax fracs (12k ft laterals, 50 stages, 2,500 lbs/ft, zonal iso). 24h IPs 1,800 BOE/d (85% oil), 15% over curve, 1.4 MBOE EUR/well. YoY +25%, ahead of Pioneer/Oxy.

Eagle Ford (18%, 45,000 BOE/d) flat QoQ, +12% YoY—deferred pads on $8 WTI-Brent spread amid $78 WTI.

Bakken/other (10%, 24,000 BOE/d) -2% QoQ on declines, offset by CO2 EOR pilot (+8% recovery). YoY flat, upstream tilt.

This resilience shines versus IEA demand softness/geopolitics. 65% 2025 oil hedged at $75 WTI. Q4 guide 252-258k BOE/d, 5-7% up on 35 TILs incl. $200M Permian JV Black Oil. Enables $800M levered FCF yearly at strips, backing 12% div hike, $300M buybacks.

Low $10-12/BOE LOE validates inventory-rich, low-cost structure.

We're also advancing cost reductions across the board.

Operator, we are now ready to open the line for questions.

Operator: [Operator Instructions] Our first question comes from Sarah Jenkins with Energy Insights. Please go ahead.

Sarah Jenkins: Thanks, and good morning, team. Could you walk us through the progress on your ESG initiatives, specifically emissions reduction targets? Investors are laser-focused on this amid the IEA's net-zero scenarios and rising TCFD disclosures.

Mark Harlan: Thanks, Sarah, great question. ESG remains a cornerstone of our strategy at Apex Energy Corp, and we're making measurable headway on emissions reductions, which directly supports our long-term value creation. I'll turn it over to our CFO, Elena Vasquez, for the details—she's been spearheading our decarbonization roadmap.

Elena Vasquez: Absolutely, Mark. Thanks, Sarah. As you know, we've committed to net-zero Scope 1 and 2 emissions by 2040, with Scope 3 ambitions aligned to industry-leading peers like Shell and TotalEnergies by 2050. Our 2023 baseline stood at 45 million metric tons of CO2 equivalent across operations, and I'm pleased to report we've achieved a 28% absolute reduction year-over-year to 32.4 million tCO2e—outpacing our 2025 interim target of 25% from the 2019 baseline of 44 million tCO2e.

On intensity metrics, vital for our expanding production base of around 250,000 boe/d scaling toward larger targets, Scope 1 and 2 GHG intensity fell 22% to 18 kg CO2e/boe, landing us in the top quartile of the Wood Mackenzie Global Upstream Decarbonization Index. Methane emissions, central given our EPA and Methane Guiding Principles pledges, dropped 52% in intensity to 0.12 kg CH4/boe—surpassing our 65% reduction goal for 2025 and beating Chevron's recent Permian marks.

Here's the breakdown by key efforts and regions, since results differ by asset type.

Technical drivers:

1. Methane control: Continuous monitoring covers 95% of assets via drone OGI and GHGSat/Kayrros satellites. Q4 alone spotted and fixed 1.2 Bcf fugitives—25,000 tCO2e averted. Pneumatics program replaced 85% high-bleed with Weatherford zero-emission units, cutting routine venting 60%.

2. Flaring cuts: Routine volumes down 68% to 0.8% of gas output (12 MMscf/d vs. 2.5% 2022). Flare recovery systems at 22 sites capture 95% for reinject/sales. Permian (450,000 boe/d ops) hit World Bank zero-flaring early via modular compressors.

3. Electrification/efficiency: Gulf of Mexico offshore 42% shore power from Ørsted renewables, Scope 2 down 15% or 1.8 million tCO2e. Onshore Eagle Ford VFDs/AI pumps reduced energy intensity 18%.

4. CCUS: Permian Apex Hub grabbed 1.2 million tCO2 in 2023 with Fluor amine tech, stored in Fusselman. Scaling to 5 million tpa by 2026 using 45Q credits and Oxy STRATOS buyers—preps for EU CBAM on exports.

By region:

- US (65% production): Permian flaring intensity 0.3% from 1.1% under Texas RRC. Eagle Ford electrification saved $45 million fuel.

- North Sea (15%): Scope 1+2 at 12 kg/boe, on track for Norway 2030 carbon tax. Rosebank all-electric subsea like Equinor Troll 3.

- Middle East JVs (10%): ADNOC UAE collab cut JV emissions 35% via shared CCUS, hitting UAE's 1 million tpa.

- Australia LNG (10%): Gorgon feedgas electrification trimmed Scope 1 22%; Scope 3 (60% footprint) tackled with 5% biofuels by 2025.

These are value-adds: $850 million decarbon CapEx (8% upstream) saved $220 million opex via efficiencies/fee avoidance—25%+ ROI. MSCI ESG to AA unlocked $2 billion green bonds at 75 bps under peers, as BlackRock/Vanguard demand S&P parity.

Ahead, 15-20% annual cuts to 2027 with $1.5 billion CCUS/hydrogen pilots like blue H2 for refiners. De-risks $100/t carbon (IEA STEPS), premiums low-carbon Asia sales. SASB disclosures keep us transparent and on track, Sarah.

Mark Harlan: Thanks, Elena. Spot on—ESG is our license to operate and grow. Sarah, any follow-ups?

Operator: Our next question comes from Brian Carter with JPMorgan. Please go ahead.

Brian Carter: Good morning. What are your expectations for capital expenditure plans and returns in 2025?

Elena Vasquez: Good morning, Brian. Thanks for the question. As I detailed in my prepared remarks, we're guiding 2025 CapEx to $6.0 to $6.4 billion, focused on high-IRR projects averaging 18-22% returns, with flexibility to adjust based on prices. This supports steady growth while prioritizing free cash flow conversion and shareholder returns. Happy to expand offline.

Operator: Our next question comes from Lisa Wong with Morgan Stanley. Please go ahead.

Lisa Wong: Could you please provide more color on the production mix changes and regional drivers quarter-over-quarter?

Tom Reilly: Good morning, Lisa. Absolutely. The QoQ oil lift to 69% mix was Permian-led, with Delaware pads outperforming on our frac tech, while gas held steady despite curtailments. Eagle Ford flat on deferrals, Bakken offset by EOR pilots. Q4 should see further oil weighting as TILs come online. Details in my earlier update, but it's all about high-margin barrels.

Operator: There are no further questions at this time. I would like to turn the conference back over to Mark Harlan for closing remarks.

Mark Harlan: Thank you, Operator. In summary, we are pleased with our performance in Q3 2024. We remain focused on executing our strategy and delivering value to our shareholders. Thank you for joining us today.

Operator: This concludes today's conference call. Thank you for your participation. You may now disconnect.
